correctness.rationale: At a=4, b=beta=c=d=e=1, f=3/2, 4<alpha<6, positive coexistence requires H=2 and P=6-alpha>0. Prey-only equation H²-3H+alpha-4=0 has roots H_- in (0,1) and H_+ in (2,3); with origin these are all four nonnegative fixed points. Origin multipliers e^(4-alpha),e^-1 are both <1; coexistence J=[[1/3,-2/3],[(6-alpha)/6,1]], trace 4/3, determinant 1-alpha/9, Jury margins alpha/9,(6-alpha)/9,(30-alpha)/9 >0, so both sinks. At prey-only H, multipliers lambda_H=1+H(3-2H)/(1+H), lambda_P=exp((H-2)/(2(1+H))). H_- is saddle. H_+ has lambda_P>1 and lambda_H crosses -1 at H=(5+sqrt41)/4, alpha_F=(29+sqrt41)/8, giving source for alpha<alpha_F, nonhyperbolic at threshold, saddle above. Algebraic checks independently recomputed original map Jacobian, exact alpha_F and inequalities; package verify.py inspected, finite parameters corroborate not replace the analytic all-alpha proof.

originality.rationale: Read complete accessible originating Seralan et al. 2023 article §§2-5, especially exact exponential map (2.3), weak-Allee restriction stated on p.22899, and local eigenvalue Lemmas 2-3. The source analyzes alpha<a beta weak regime; for alpha>a beta the origin is a sink, whereas its weak-regime Lemma 2 says origin always saddle. Therefore its weak-region classification does not imply strong-Allee bistability, four-equilibria region, or alpha_F. Al Khabyah et al. use a different Euler-discretized strong-Allee equation; Cai et al. use a continuous diffusive counterpart (the latter was not fully accessible). Earlier Resultary Ricker source-criterion correction addresses different weak-regime stability, not this exact family.

value.rationale: Exact local coexistence/extinction bistability and a source-to-saddle transition of the upper prey-only equilibrium resolve a natural qualitative strong-Allee regime in the same exponential ecological map. This provides all fixed points and their spectral types for a connected open parameter interval, not just one numerical witness. No global basin partition, ecological realism, or nonlinear flip bifurcation is claimed.

limitations: Local spectral classification and open local basins only; other attractors or basin boundaries not ruled out.
At alpha_F a multiplier is -1; no nonlinear flip-period-two theorem claimed.
